Opposite Party
 Mr. M.R. Mishra, Asc
 Coram:
Justice Savitri Ratho

Order
16.04.2024 Order No. (Through hybrid mode) 03 1.

This is the second application of the petitioner under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with Reamal P.S. Case No.343 of 2023 corresponding to C.T. Case No.639 of 2023 in the file of the learned J.M.F.C., Reamal in respect of which trial has commenced in the court of the learned Assistant Sessions Judge-cum-STC, Deogarh in S.T. Case No.
6/27 of 2023-24 under Sections 376 (2) (n)/506 of IPC and Sections 67/67 (A)/66 (E) of the I.T.
Act.
2.

The earlier application of the petitioner as BLAPL No. 624 of 2024 had been dismissed by me on 07.02.2024 but liberty had been granted to the petitioner to move for bail afresh after examination of the victim girl in the trial.

The copy of the deposition of the victim who has been examined as P.W.1 in the trial has been annexed to this bail application and the deposition of her grand-mother P.W.2 and her uncle P.W.3 have also been annexed to the bail application.
3. After recording of the evidence of the victim on 16.02.2024, the petitioner had moved the learned trial court for bail and the same has been rejected on 26.02.2024.
Learned court below found that the victim, informant and her grand mother have not supported the prosecution case and have turned hostile.
But in view of the prima facie evidence in respect of commission of offences punishable under Sections 67 (A)/66 (E) of the I.T. Act, the learned court below has rejected the prayer for bail.

4. The prosecution allegation in brief is that on 18.03.2023 while the victim was going to her college,
the petitioner seeing her alone, seduced her and compelled to have physical relation with him.
He recorded such act and compelled the victim to have sexual relation with him on a number of times threatening to make the video and photos viral and to kill her.
On 20.10.2023, the petitioner opened a fake face book account and uploaded some nude photos and videos of the victim in between 6.30 a.m. to 7.00 p.m. and thereafter deleted the same.

sentences.text: Mr. J.K. Panda, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the petitioner and the victim were in love.

But due to some misunderstanding, the F.I.R. has been registered for which the victim who has been examined in the trial has stated that she has not filed any F.I.R. in the Police Station and stated that she is in love with the petitioner and intends to marry him and her parents had entangled the petitioner in a false case as they were against their marriage.

He further submits that since the examination of the victim, her uncle and grand-mother are over and the petitioner is in custody since 04.11.2023, no useful purpose will be served by detaining the petitioner any further in jail custody.
6. I have perused the depositions of P.Ws.1, 2 and 3 which have been filed along with the bail application.
All 3 witnesses have been cross-examined by the prosecution as they have not supported the prosecution case.

7. Mr. S.S. Mohapatra, learned Additional Standing Counsel opposes the prayer for bail stating that the victim had made specific allegations against the petitioner in the F.I.R., the statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. and in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
But apparently with the hope to marry the petitioner, she has not supported the prosecution case.
He further submits that there are ample materials in the case diary which establish the commission of offences punishable under Section 67-A, 66-E and 67 of the I.T. Act against the petitioner.
8. Considering the depositions of P.Ws. 1 to 3, more particularly of the victim P.W.1 and her age, I am inclined to allow the prayer for bail of the petitioner.

9. The petitioner- Suresh Behera shall be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be fixed by the learned Court below in seisin over the matter, including the following conditions :
(i) He will not indulge in any criminal activity while on bail.
(ii) He will not tamper or try to influence prosecution witnesses while on bail.
(iii) He will appear before the IIC, Reamal Police Station, Deogarh once a week between 5.00 p.m. to 6.00 p.m. till completion of investigation.
(iii) He will not venture near the house of the victim or try to contact her.
(iv) He will remain present in the trial Court on each date it if fixed for trial unless his appearance is dispensed with by the learned trial Court under Section 317 Cr.P.C. on any particular day.
10. Violation of any condition will entail in cancellation of bail.
11. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
